subject: ss-haematology
title: Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia: classification, risk and key therapies

steps.tx: **Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia** (ALL) is a malignancy of immature lymphoid progenitors. Lymphoblasts crowd out normal marrow, causing anaemia, neutropenia and thrombocytopenia. A bone marrow biopsy is essential to confirm acute leukaemia and separate ALL from AML. Flow cytometry then assigns lineage: B-lineage cells express CD19, CD22, CD79a and PAX5, while T-lineage cells express cytoplasmic or surface CD3. A marker is called positive when more than 20 percent of cells stain.

rows: Early precursor often lacks CD1a and CD8

steps.tx: **Philadelphia-positive ALL** carries t(9;22) producing BCR::ABL1, confirmed by karyotype, FISH or RT-PCR. It needs a **tyrosine kinase inhibitor** from induction onwards, such as dasatinib or imatinib in paediatric-inspired protocols or ponatinib in adults. **Ph-like ALL** is BCR::ABL1 negative but shares similar lesions, such as CRLF2 or ABL-class fusions, and needs molecular testing to identify. Misclassifying it as Ph-positive is a classic trap.
steps.say: Philadelphia-positive ALL carries the t(9;22) translocation producing BCR::ABL1, confirmed by karyotype, FISH or RT-PCR. It needs a tyrosine kinase inhibitor from induction onwards, such as dasatinib or imatinib in paediatric-inspired protocols, or ponatinib in adults. Ph-like ALL is BCR::ABL1 negative but shares similar lesions, such as CRLF2 or ABL-class fusions, and needs molecular testing to identify. Misclassifying it as Ph-positive is a classic trap.

steps.tx: **Minimal residual disease** (MRD) is the most important prognostic factor during therapy. A molecular complete remission after induction means MRD of 0.01 percent or less and predicts disease-free survival near 70 percent, compared with under 40 percent when MRD is positive. In paediatric B-ALL, end-induction MRD of 0.01 percent or higher escalates a standard-risk patient to high-risk therapy. Persistent MRD is an indication for blinatumomab.
steps.say: Minimal residual disease is the most important prognostic factor during therapy. A molecular complete remission after induction means MRD of 0.01 percent or less, and predicts disease-free survival near 70 percent. When MRD is positive, disease-free survival falls below 40 percent. In paediatric B-ALL, end-induction MRD of 0.01 percent or higher escalates a standard-risk patient to high-risk therapy. Persistent MRD is an indication for blinatumomab.

steps.tx: **Blinatumomab**, a bispecific T-cell engager targeting CD19, is used for CD19-positive relapsed disease and for persistent MRD. In ECOG 1910, adding blinatumomab consolidation to chemotherapy in MRD-negative adults improved survival. **Inotuzumab ozogamicin**, an anti-CD22 antibody-drug conjugate, suits CD22-positive disease but carries a risk of sinusoidal obstruction syndrome, so ursodiol is given when bridging to transplant. CAR-T tisagenlecleucel is licensed for patients aged 25 or younger with relapsed B-ALL.
